Ch 5 · Arithmetic Progressions — Practice

MCQs

The 10th term of the AP 2, 7, 12, … is: (a) 45 (b) 47 (c) 50 (d) 52

(b) 47. a₁₀ = 2 + 9(5).

The sum of the first 10 natural numbers is: (a) 45 (b) 50 (c) 55 (d) 100

(c) 55. n(n+1)/2 = 10 × 11/2.

S₅ − S₄ equals: (a) the 5th term (b) the 4th term (c) the 9th term (d) zero

(a) The 5th term. That is what aₙ = Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁ means.

Written questions

2 marks Find the 20th term from the last term of the AP 3, 8, 13, …, 253.

Counting from the end, the AP is 253, 248, 243, … with a = 253 and d = −5.
20th term = 253 + 19(−5) = 158.

3 marks Which term of the AP 3, 15, 27, 39, … will be 132 more than its 54th term?

54th term = 3 + 53(12) = 639.
Required term = 639 + 132 = 771.
3 + (n − 1)12 = 771 gives (n − 1)12 = 768, so n = 65.

3 marks If the sum of the first n terms of an AP is 3n² + 5n, find its 10th term.

aₙ = Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁.
S₁₀ = 300 + 50 = 350 and S₉ = 243 + 45 = 288.
a₁₀ = 350 − 288 = 62.

5 marks A sum of Rs 700 is to be used to give seven cash prizes, each prize being Rs 20 less than its preceding prize. Find the value of each prize.

Seven prizes in AP with d = −20 and S₇ = 700.
700 = (7/2)[2a + 6(−20)] = (7/2)(2a − 120).
200 = 2a − 120, so a = 160.
The prizes are Rs 160, 140, 120, 100, 80, 60 and 40.
